history.summary: Arulmigu Sugavaneswarar Temple at Mettu Agraharam, Cherry Road near the Fort area, in central Salem city (CSV town 'Salem' is correct; ~2-acre compact shrine with a small three-tiered east-facing Rajagopuram). Dedicated to Shiva as Sugavaneswarar ('Parrot-Shiva') with consort Swarnambika. Legend: Brahma cursed the sage Suka (Suga Brahma Rishi, of parrot voice/face) into a parrot; worshipping Shiva here, the parrots hid in an anthill from a hunter whose weapon struck the lingam — tilting it and leaving the scar still visible — and Suka shielded the lingam with his wings, attaining liberation; the forest was hence Sukavanam. The swayambhu lingam tilts slightly to the right. Saint Avvaiyar is said to have performed miracles here and married off her adopted daughter in this shrine, attended by the Chola, Chera and Pandya monarchs (legend). The Saivite saint poets sang its glories; the sthala puranam claims it as a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Sundara Nayanar, though that song is untraced (verify). Arunagirinathar sang of Subrahmanya here. Inscriptions: Uttama Chola (9th c.) and Parantaka Chola (as 'Kizhi vana nathar alayam', Tamil for Sukavaneswara). Notables: the Amanduga ('frogless') well in the 80-pillared hall's north — Adisesha is said to reside there and frogs die in its water (legend); a shrine to Avvaiyar; the 63 Nayanmars; Mysore-dynasty traces; a temple tank across the lane. One of five swayambhu Shiva sthalams on the banks of the Manimuthar river — worship at all five in a day is believed to remove sins (verify).
